prerequisites: Basic knowledge of business and corporate management
Successful completion of the StEOP (Study Introductory and Orientation Phase)

learning_outcomes.text: Explain problems arising in the financing of new and young companies due to asymmetric information between company founders on the one hand and investors on the other (Agency Theory).
Quantify the impact of capital structure on a company's financially sustainable development and calculate the impact on financing costs (short-, medium-, and long-term).
Decompose business risk into the influence of different risk factors and determine market risk as well as idiosyncratic risk.
Estimate capital costs for a new company using benchmarking from financial statements and financial market data of comparable companies.
Explain the business and investment models of Venture Capital funds and the implications of Venture Capital financing on the development of a young company.
Explain the various terms and aspects considered in connection with the modern understanding of sustainability.
Assess the sustainability performance of companies from the perspective of 'double materiality'.
Understand the most important regulations for corporate sustainability reporting in the EU.
Integrate sustainability goals into corporate management and subsequently manage them.
Cooperatively solve tasks in individual and teamwork.
Present complex content in an audience-appropriate manner.

Precisely and increasingly independently apply instruments for planning and control tasks in financial and sustainability management. Critically and constructively discuss calculation methods and solution approaches within the framework of peer feedback.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of evaluating a business concept
The LifeCycle from a newly founded company to an IPO or trade sale.
Communication with investors / Documents for a successful 'pitch'.
Concept of Economic Profit and the incentive effect of management compensation contracts.
Impact of capital structure and ownership structure on company development in different phases of the company's lifecycle.
Venture Capital financing, milestone-oriented management, and the path-dependent dynamics of control rights in young companies.
Fundamentals of the increasing importance of sustainability in corporate management
Terminology, concepts, and elements of the modern understanding of sustainability
Most important EU regulations for sustainability (reporting)
Preparation and analysis of sustainability reports
Integration of sustainability into corporate management (PDCA cycle)
teaching_methods: Lectures on the theoretical foundations and basic instruments of the above-mentioned chapters, as well as illustration of their application with concrete examples.
Practicing what has been learned by independently solving exercise examples.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with calculation examples and theory questions
Continuous assessment through regular homework and tests
